briefdescription.para: Replace a select operand based on an equality comparison with the identity constant of a binop.
This folds: select (icmp eq (and X, C1)), TC, FC iff C1 is a power 2 and the difference between TC and FC is a power-of-2.

detaileddescription.para: To something like: (shr (and (X, C1)), (log2(C1) - log2(TC-FC))) + FC Or: (shl (and (X, C1)), (log2(TC-FC) - log2(C1))) + FC With some variations depending if FC is larger than TC, or the shift isn't needed, or the bit widths don't match.

briefdescription.para: We want to turn code that looks like this: C = or A, B D = select cond, C, A into: C = select cond, B, 0 D = or A, C.

detaileddescription.para: Assuming that the specified instruction is an operand to the select, return a bitmask indicating which operands of this instruction are foldable if they equal the other incoming value of the select.

briefdescription.para: We want to turn: (select (icmp eq (and X, Y), 0), (and (lshr X, Z), 1), 1) into: zext (icmp ne i32 (and X, (or Y, (shl 1, Z))), 0) Note: Z may be 0 if lshr is missing.

detaileddescription.para: Worst-case scenario is that we will replace 5 instructions with 5 different instructions, but we got rid of select.

briefdescription.para: We want to turn: (select (icmp eq (and X, C1), 0), 0, (shl [nsw/nuw] X, C2)); iff C1 is a mask and the number of its leading zeros is equal to C2 into: shl X, C2.
We want to turn: (select (icmp sgt x, C), lshr (X, Y), ashr (X, Y)); iff C s>= -1 (select (icmp slt x, C), ashr (X, Y), lshr (X, Y)); iff C s>= 0 into: ashr (X, Y)

We want to turn: (select (icmp eq (and X, C1), 0), Y, (BinOp Y, C2)) into: IF C2 u>= C1 (BinOp Y, (shl (and X, C1), C3)) ELSE (BinOp Y, (lshr (and X, C1), C3)) iff: 0 on the RHS is the identity value (i.e add, xor, shl, etc...) C1 and C2 are both powers of 2 where: IF C2 u>= C1 C3 = Log(C2) - Log(C1) ELSE C3 = Log(C1) - Log(C2)

detaileddescription.para:
This transform handles cases where:
The icmp predicate is inverted
The select operands are reversed
The magnitude of C2 and C1 are flipped
